name: Orders, Brotherhoods and Secret Societies
description: Monks with swords, masons with secrets and clubs that shaped a nation: the groups that people joined by oath, and the legends that grew around them.

checkpoints.name: Monks and warrior orders
checkpoints.note: Monasteries such as Shaolin and the Benedictines gave religious life a rule, while in the Holy Land the Hospitallers and the Templars joined prayer to war and the Assassins held their mountain forts.

checkpoints.name: Friars, knights and the Church
checkpoints.note: New orders of friars, the Franciscans and Dominicans, worked in the cities, and the Teutonic Knights ruled the Baltic. In 1312 the Templars were dissolved, and in 1540 the Jesuits were founded.

checkpoints.name: The age of lodges and clubs
checkpoints.note: Quakers, Sikh Khalsa and Masonic lodges formed outside the established churches. In Birmingham and Bavaria, clubs of reasoning men met in secret or by moonlight, and some were banned.

checkpoints.name: Modern brotherhoods
checkpoints.note: In the modern age secret societies such as Skull and Bones, fraternal orders such as the Knights of Columbus and new reform groups such as the Fabians and Alcoholics Anonymous mix charity, ritual and politics.
